marks.gloss_en: לדבריהם דרבי אליעזר ורבי עקיבא קאמר ליה, וליה לא סבירא ליה -- he explained within the tannaim's framework; it shows nothing of his own view
Rav Adda bar Ahava: a gentile who carved a kav[-measure] in a log -- a Jew may kindle it on a Festival
one may not light with an unsinged wick -- so one may not light with it
דתנן: שלש על שלש שאמרו חוץ מן המלל, דברי רבי שמעון; וחכמים אומרים שלש על שלש מכוונות -- 'exactly three by three' is the Sages' impurity measure
if R' Eliezer's reason is the unsinged wick, then Rav Yosef's 'three by three exactly' -- for what halakha is it?
לענין טומאה -- it concerns impurity (= p_rav_yosef_leinyan_tumah)
Rava: R' Eliezer's reason is that one may not light with a wick that is not singed, nor with rags that are not singed
דרב אכל תמרי ושדא קשייתא לבוכיא, אמר ליה רבי חייא: כנגדו ביום טוב אסור -- Rav's statement was drawn from this exchange (no SupportKind names a narrated precedent)
this [statement] of Rav was not stated explicitly but by inference
תא שמע: כי אתא רב לבבל אכל תמרי ושדא קשייתא לחיותא -- מאי לאו בפרסייאתא, ולא קבלה? -- Persian dates leave bare pits, so throwing them shows he did not accept
לא, בארמייאתא -- הואיל וחזי אגב אימייהו: Aramean dates, whose pits are fit by virtue of the fruit left on them
Rav did not accept [R' Chiyya's ruling] from him
דאמר רב מתנה אמר רב: עצים שנשרו מן הדקל לתנור ביום טוב, מרבה עצים מוכנין ומסיקן
לרבי יהודה... כיון דאדליק בהו פורתא הוה ליה שברי כלים, וכי קא מהפך -- באיסורא קא מהפך? -- once a vessel has burnt a little it is broken vessels, so turning it over handles something forbidden
דעבד כדרב מתנה -- he adds prepared wood, as Rav Mattana taught of fallen palm-wood (= p_avad_kidrav_matana); unmarked, so the stam's, though read as Rav Yosef's reply
Rav Mattana in Rav's name: wood that fell from a palm into the oven on the Festival -- one adds prepared wood and kindles them
ואזדא רבי אליעזר לטעמיה, דתנן: ...בין מן המוכן ובין שאין מן המוכן טמא -- R' Eliezer's impurity of the wick follows his view on a cloth under three by three (no SupportKind names דתנן)
ורבי עקיבא לטעמיה, דתנן: רבי עקיבא אומר... שלא מן המוכן טהור -- R' Akiva's purity of the wick follows his view on the unprepared cloth
a cloth under three by three fitted to plug the bath, pour from the pot or wipe the millstone, if prepared [for it], is impure
Rav: kindling with broken vessels, with date pits after eating the dates, and with nut shells after eating the nuts, are disputed -- R' Yehuda forbids, R' Shimon permits
at first it was a vessel and now it is a broken vessel, so it is nolad [newly come into being] and forbidden
Rav Hamnuna: here [the mishna of the folded, unsinged wick] deals with less than three by three; they taught here of the leniencies of rags
